verses.text: Yahweh said to Moses, “Now you shall see what I will do to Pharaoh, for by a strong hand he shall let them go, and by a strong hand he shall drive them out of his land.”
God spoke to Moses, and said to him, “I am Yahweh;
and I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, as God Almighty; but by my name Yahweh I was not known to them.
I have also established my covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan, the land of their travels, in which they lived as aliens.
Moreover I have heard the groaning of the children of Israel, whom the Egyptians keep in bondage, and I have remembered my covenant.

Therefore tell the children of Israel, ‘I am Yahweh, and I will bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians, and I will rid you out of their bondage, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm, and with great judgments:
and I will take you to me for a people, and I will be to you a God; and you shall know that I am Yahweh your God, who brings you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians.
I will bring you into the land which I swore to give to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob; and I will give it to you for a heritage: I am Yahweh.’”
Moses spoke so to the children of Israel, but they didn’t listen to Moses for anguish of spirit, and for cruel bondage.
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Go in, speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt, that he let the children of Israel go out of his land.”
Moses spoke before Yahweh, saying, “Behold, the children of Israel haven’t listened to me. How then shall Pharaoh listen to me, who am of uncircumcised lips?”
Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Aaron, and gave them a command to the children of Israel, and to Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.
These are the heads of their fathers’ houses. The sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel: Hanoch, and Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi; these are the families of Reuben.
The sons of Simeon: Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanite woman; these are the families of Simeon.
These are the names of the sons of Levi according to their generations: Gershon, and Kohath, and Merari; and the years of the life of Levi were one hundred thirty-seven years.
The sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei, according to their families.
The sons of Kohath: Amram, and Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel; and the years of the life of Kohath were one hundred thirty-three years.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These are the families of the Levites according to their generations.
Amram took Jochebed his father’s sister to himself as wife; and she bore him Aaron and Moses: and the years of the life of Amram were a hundred and thirty-seven years.
The sons of Izhar: Korah, and Nepheg, and Zichri.
The sons of Uzziel: Mishael, and Elzaphan, and Sithri.
Aaron took Elisheba, the daughter of Amminadab, the sister of Nahshon, as his wife; and she bore him Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
The sons of Korah: Assir, and Elkanah, and Abiasaph; these are the families of the Korahites.
Eleazar Aaron’s son took one of the daughters of Putiel as his wife; and she bore him Phinehas. These are the heads of the fathers’ houses of the Levites according to their families.
These are that Aaron and Moses, to whom Yahweh said, “Bring out the children of Israel from the land of Egypt according to their armies.”
These are those who spoke to Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring out the children of Israel from Egypt. These are that Moses and Aaron.
On the day when Yahweh spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying, “I am Yahweh. Speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt all that I speak to you.”
Moses said before Yahweh, “Behold, I am of uncircumcised lips, and how shall Pharaoh listen to me?”

footnotes.content: What a shift in Yahweh's tone—from the delays Moses faced with Pharaoh, now comes a word of absolute certainty. He will do it. The strong hand that seemed hidden will become visible, undeniable. When all our persuading fails, the Lord moves by His own power alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Here Yahweh speaks His own name aloud—not as a command, but as an introduction, as one making Himself known. In that name lies His power and His promise. To know His name is to know His faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob knew Him as *God Almighty*—El Shaddai—but now He reveals Himself as Yahweh, the God who acts in history, who remembers and delivers. Every generation knows Him more deeply than the one before.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The covenant made long ago was not forgotten, though centuries have passed and the patriarchs sleep. What He promised remains firm. Canaan still waits. This is the heart of it—He keeps His word across the ages.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The groaning of enslaved Israel reaches His ear. He hears what the world thinks is silent suffering. He remembers. Not because He forgot—because the time of remembering and acting has come. Our cries are never lost on Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Four great *I will* promises unfold here: bring out, rid of bondage, redeem, judge. Each verb paints a different face of deliverance—rescue, freedom, costly redemption, divine justice. To be brought out is to be remade.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From slaves in Egypt to the people of God—that is the movement here. Not just freedom from, but belonging to. To know that Yahweh is *your* God transforms everything. We learn His name not in books but in being brought near to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The promise to Abraham circles back. The land sworn to the fathers becomes their heritage—their possession, their home. What seemed like a distant dream across four centuries becomes real land under their feet. Yahweh ties the past to the future.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even when the Word comes, Israel cannot hear it. Their spirits are broken under the weight of bondage. Sometimes the cruelest chain is the one that crushes hope itself. Yet Yahweh does not withdraw His promise because His people cannot receive it yet.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: After Israel's refusal, Yahweh speaks again to Moses. The Lord does not turn back from His purpose. He meets His servant in the darkness of discouragement and gives him fresh direction. Faithfulness is not shaken by faithlessness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Go speak to Pharaoh. Moses is sent again, not because the last mission worked—it didn't—but because the Lord sends him. Some tasks are not measured by success but by obedience. We go not knowing the outcome, only trusting the One who sends us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses speaks what feels true: Israel won't listen, so why would Pharaoh? He calls himself uncircumcised of lips—inadequate, unprepared. How often do we stay silent because we believe the case against ourselves? Yet the Lord is not asking for eloquence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh gives a charge to Moses and Aaron together—and extends it to both Israel and Pharaoh. Everyone has a role in this unfolding story. The Lord is orchestrating something larger than any one person's weakness or resistance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now comes the genealogy—the families of Israel laid bare by name and line. Each name carries a history, a story of who they are. They are not nameless slaves but the sons of Jacob, traceable back through generations. God knows His people by name.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Simeon is named, though he will fade as the story progresses. Every tribe is recorded, every son counted. Yahweh's attention does not favor the famous—all are held in His memory, all are His.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Levi's name is given, and his line established. He lived a long life—137 years—to see his sons multiply and his legacy spread. Sometimes we inherit not land first, but a calling that ripples through our families.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons of Gershon—another branch of Levi's household. These families will become guardians of sacred things. Their lineage is their priesthood, their naming a kind of ordination.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Kohath lived 133 years. His line includes Amram—father of Moses. Even here, before Moses appears, his ancestry is woven into Israel's priestly genealogy. The Lord prepares His servants before they are born.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons of Merari complete the three branches of Levi. From one man came three families, each serving in the sanctuary. One calling, many expressions of faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Amram took Jochebed as wife—his father's sister—and she bore Aaron and Moses. Here is the family line of the greatest deliverer and his brother the first priest. The Lord uses ordinary human families to accomplish extraordinary things.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons of Izhar named: Korah will later rebel against Moses. Even his name is recorded here, not yet in shame. Every person has a place in God's story before their choices write the rest.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three sons of Uzziel, each named, each known. In the genealogy's careful recording, we see that God numbers not just the famous but every soul. All are numbered in His account.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Aaron married Elisheba and fathered Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. These sons will serve as priests—sacred vessels—yet some will stumble. Even priestly families are human, needing grace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons of Korah are named here. Their father will rebel, but the sons will not all follow him into darkness. Families carry both light and shadow. One person's failure does not seal all who share their blood.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eleazar married and fathered Phinehas. The priestly line continues, each generation inheriting calling from the one before. Phinehas will become known for his zeal. The Lord prepares faithfulness across generations.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Here the genealogy turns—these are Aaron and Moses, to whom Yahweh spoke. After listing their families, their descent, now comes the reason: they are the ones called to lead. Lineage finds its purpose in calling.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses and Aaron—the speakers to Pharaoh. Their names are repeated with emphasis. They are sent. They are named. They are known. The Lord does not send unnamed workers but calls them by name.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "On the day when Yahweh spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt"—time is marked by the Lord's word. Our lives are not measured by what men think but by when and where God speaks to us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo: the Lord says "I am Yahweh" and asks Moses to speak all He commands to Pharaoh. How many times do we hesitate to speak truth because we fear the listener's power? Yet our role is simply to speak what He gives us—He answers for the outcome.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses' final objection circles back to his first—uncircumcised lips. He stands before Yahweh with the same weakness he carried before. The Lord does not answer by removing the weakness but by presence and calling regardless.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
